experiment: SCARCITY SHOWDOWN: the honest head-to-head vs a REAL SOTA baseline. e9 showed Mem0-style memory holds a SINGLE number, so the measurement advantage can only appear under SCARCE budget + MANY competing fields, where every method keeps only a few facts and WHICH ones is the question. At an IDENTICAL per-hop carry budget B=25: free_text (compress all M into prose) vs mem0 (B-word extracted fact-list, Mem0 salience heuristic) vs ours (B split into verbatim [SLOTS] for the P measured-most-fragile facts + compressed [NOTES] for the rest). Metric: TOTAL survival over all M=12 facts at depth K=4.
regime: e7 MEDIUM regime (M=12, K=4) where free_text per-type survival has a real gradient (pref/num worst, negation best) -> a non-obvious worst type exists for measurement to exploit and for Mem0's fragility-blind salience to miss. C=10 chains, P=4 protection budget.
why_fair: All three arms bounded by the SAME per-hop budget B=25 words; they differ only in ALLOCATION strategy within B. ours' slots eat ~4 words each so notes get B-4P; mem0 uses all B for its list; free_text uses all B for prose. Calibration for ours = leave-one-chain-out per-type free_text survival (measured, no peeking at the held-out chain).
sota_fidelity: mem0 = faithful minimal Mem0 (extract FACT_RETRIEVAL_PROMPT paraphrase + merge ADD/UPDATE/DELETE), the scout-designated most-important baseline and canonical salience-based memory. It has NO per-type retention measurement -> keeps generically-salient facts.

PRE_REGISTERED_READOUT.BEATS_SOTA: ours TOTAL survival > mem0 (ours_minus_mem0 > 0, ideally with the gap tracking oracle and beating folk/random) -> measurement-driven allocation beats the deployed SOTA memory's salience heuristic under scarce budget, because Mem0 is blind to the non-obvious per-type fragility ranking. This is the honest, defensible 'beat SOTA' result: same budget, better allocation.
PRE_REGISTERED_READOUT.TIE: ours ~ mem0 -> Mem0's salience heuristic happens to allocate as well as measurement here (e.g. it also keeps the fragile facts) -> honest: no allocation advantage over SOTA in this regime; the contribution is the characterization + measurement necessity vs the naive folk baseline only. Report without a SOTA-beating claim.
PRE_REGISTERED_READOUT.SOTA_WINS: mem0 > ours -> the real memory pipeline outperforms our slot allocation (e.g. mem0's retrieval recovers more than exempt-slots+starved-notes) -> our method is not competitive with deployed memory; pivot to pure characterization. Report honestly.

predictions.point: free_text lowest total. mem0 mid (keeps salient facts but is fragility-blind -> under-protects the non-obvious worst type). ours highest, tracking ref_oracle@P and beating ref_folk@P/ref_random@P, and > mem0 by a positive margin. The load-bearing reason: on Sonnet the worst type is non-obvious (e7: preference), so a salience heuristic mis-allocates while measurement targets it.
predictions.risk: (1) mem0's fact-list may keep MORE than P facts within B (lists are compact) -> mem0 total could exceed ours if ours starves its notes; then TIE/SOTA_WINS. (2) multi-slot (P=4) not previously validated live -> slots may not all hold like the single slot did (e8b) under a tight notes budget; if slots bleed, ours drops. (3) n=10 chains, temp=0 -> directional, no CIs. (4) budget-fairness (slots exempt vs mem0 list) is approximate; report as such.
predictions.honest_limits: single model (Sonnet); one regime (M=12/K=4) and one P=4; faithful-minimal Mem0 (no vector DB, but with M=12 facts retrieval is not the bottleneck -- the extract/merge budget is); this tests allocation-under-scarcity, not single-fact survival (e9 settled that).
